sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:
On 27-04-2019 at about 11.30 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on two wheeler bearing No.KA-06-EM-122 on Old NH-4, Sira Road, when he reached (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.3841/2019 Opposite to Maruthi Rice Mill, near Sridevi Hostel,
Lingapura, Tumkur.
At that time, the driver of KSRTC bearing Reg.No.KA-06-F-1010 came in high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner vehicle.
Due to which petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over his body.

Immediately he was shifted to Shridevi Institute of Medical Science and Research Hospital, Sira, wherein X-rays were taken which revealed fracture injuries and then referred to NIMHANS Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 28.04.2019 to 30.04.2019 and then referred to Victora Hospital, wherein also he took treatment as inpatient from 01.05.2019 to 07.05.2019 and after necessary treatment he was discharged with an advise to take followup treatment.

entities.text: Shridevi Institute of Medical Science and Research Hospital, Sira
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as mason and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.3841/2019
The petitioner has lost his earning capacity and cannot do his normal work prior to the accident.
The accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-F-1010.
The jurisdictional Police have registered a Criminal Case against the driver of KSRTC Bus in Cr.No.109/2019 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC.
After investigation the Police have filed Charge Sheet against the driver of KSRTC Bus.
The respondent being RC Owner and Insurer of the KSRTC Bus is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
petitioner constrained to file a petition for compensation.
3. After service of notice the respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel and filed its written statement.

The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 is as under:

sentences.text: This respondent has denied the contents of claim (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.3841/2019 petition specifically and categorically.

It has contended that the petition is bad for mis-joinder and non-joinder of necessary parties i.e., the rider of TVS Excel bearing Reg.No.KA-06-EM-122 was solely responsible for the cause of alleged accident.
The owner and insurer of Motor Cycle are necessary parties.

The driver of the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-06-F-1010 was no way responsible for the alleged accident,
consequently respondent is not a necessary party to the proceedings.
It has specifically denied the manner of accident, the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
It has also denied the injuries sustained, treatment taken and expenses incurred towards medicine.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
With this ground it has prayed to dismiss the petition.
The 2nd respondent subsequently added on the basis of written statement filed by 1st respondent with regard to non joinder of necessary party.

The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 is as under:
This respondent has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
This respondent has admitted the petition averments with regard to accident and treatment taken by the petitioner.
This respondent has also admitted he was the rider of the motor cycle bearing Regn No.KA-06-EM-122 as on the date of accident.
This respondent further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and hence prayed for rejecting the petition.
4. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues:

bearing Reg.No.KA-06-F-1010 came in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing any of the traffic rule and regulations and dashed against the petitioner vehicle.

Due to impact, petitioner fell down and grievous injuries in the alleged ?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum of compensation?
from whom?

She also relied documents at Ex.P4 to P17.

The Ex.P4 is the FIR, Ex.P5 is the complaint, Ex.P6 is the Spot Panchanama, Ex.P7 is the IMV Report, Ex.P8 is the Charge Sheet, Ex.P9 is the Medico Legal Certificate, Ex.P10 is the discharge summary, Ex.P11 & 12 are the Notarized copy of Aadhaar card,

A perusal of above records it shows that one Venkatesh S/o.Dasappa has lodged First Information before Traffic Police Tumkuru alleging that on 27.04.2019 at about 11.30 am., the petitioner and other two persons were met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of driver of KSRTC Bus, bearing Reg.No.KA-06-F-1010 while petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in TVS motor cycle and sustained grievous injuries.
On the basis of this first Information the Tumkuru Traffic Police have registered the case in Cr.No.109/2019 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279, 337 & 304 A of IPC.

Thereafter, the Investigating Officer had conducted the Investigation and filed the Charge Sheet against the driver of KSRTC Bus by name Karegappa.B.Hirehatti. for the offence punishable U/ Sec.279, 338 & 304 A of IPC.

The PW2/wife of petitioner has stated the cause of the accident in her chief-examination affidavit.
The PW2 was subjected to cross-examined but nothing was elicited (SCCH-9) 11 MVC.No.3841/2019 to disbelieve her evidence with regard to accident.
Admittedly this PW2 was not an eye witness to the accident.
However the Ex.P7 MV Report discloses that the some parts of motor cycle as well KSRTC were damaged.
It shows that these two vehicles were involved in the accident.
13. The 1st respondent in order to prove its case it has examined the driver of KSRTC Bus as RW1.

The RW1 in his chief-examination affidavit mainly contended that when he was proceeding as a driver in KSRTC Bus at that time the rider of TVS motor cycle came from opposite side and caused the accident.
The accident in question was caused by the rider of TVS motor cycle.
He never caused the accident.
It is material to note that this RW1 has not challenged the charge sheet filed against him.
If at all, the rider of TVS motor cycle caused the accident what prevented this RW1 to file complaint against rider of motor cycle.
There is nothing on record to show this RW1 has filed (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.3841/2019 complaint against rider of motor cycle.
Therefore, only on self swearing statement it cannot be held that the accident was not caused by the driver of KSRTC Bus.

Apart from this in a claim petition arising out of the accident the proving of negligence of offending vehicle is only preponderance of probabilities and not standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt as required in criminal case.

This principles of law was laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum & Others V/s Satbir & others).
14.

The argument advanced by the learned counsel for 1 st respondent holds no water.

Therefore, the documents relied by petitioner and oral evidence of PW2 clearly establishes that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligence act of the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-F-1010.
Now it can safely be concluded, that the injuries were caused to the petitioner due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the KSRTC Bus.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that the petitioner has proved issue No.1.
Hence, I answered issue No.1 in the affirmative.
(SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.3841/2019 15. ISSUE NO.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation the Tribunal has to look into several facts like injuries,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant, charges, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc. let me discuss one by one:
a) TOWARDS INJURY, PAIN AND SUFFERING:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and discharged with an advise to take follow up treatment.

In order to prove injuries caused to him he has produced wound certificate/Ex.P9,
which reveals that petitioner has sustained injuries and doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injury.

The record also shows that the petitioner took treatment in the hospital as an inpatient (SCCH-9) 15 MVC.No.3841/2019 and the petitioner has examined doctor by name Dr.Shailesh.A.V.Rao as PW1 to prove the disability.
The PW1 got marked documents at Ex.P11 & 12.
The PW.1 has assessed the disability of petitioner.
Therefore by considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.30,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and sufferings.
b) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at hospital and produced medical bills marked at Ex.P14 for Rs.13,168/-.
The record shows that there is no serious dispute about these medical bills.
Hence the Tribunal is of the view that petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.13,168/- is just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
c ) T O W A R D S F O O D , E X T R A N O U R I S H M E N T , A N D ( S C C H - 9 ) 1 6 MVC.No.3841/2019

During the time of treatment the petitioner also required good food and extra nourishment.

Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/- per day for 7 days to a sum of Rs.7,000/- is just and reasonable towards food extra nourishment and medical attendant.
d) TOWARDS CONVEYANCE:
According to petitioner, he spent some amount for conveyance while he was admitted in the hospital till discharge from the hospital.
It is true that the petitioner has not produced any document to show he has incurred expenses for conveyance.
However, it is quite natural that if any person admitted in the hospital he might have spent some amount towards conveyance.

Therefore,
considering the injuries and treatment taken by the petitioner this tribunal is of the (SCCH-9) 17 MVC.No.3841/2019 opinion that Rs.10,000/- is just and proper towards conveyance charges.
e) TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner contended that he was working as mason and Rs.25,000/-pm, as a salary.
In order to prove his income he has not produced any documents to show that he was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
In the absence of positive documents regarding his occupation and income this Tribunal will consider notional income.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, fixed notional income for the year 2019 at Rs.14,000/- p.m., for determination of income before Lokadalath for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Principal Benches, Bengaluru.

So in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it is just and proper to this Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.
Accordingly, the notional income of (SCCH-9) 18 MVC.No.3841/2019 petitioner during the year 2019 treated as Rs.14,000/- p.m., as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case this tribunal held that petitioner is entitled to Rs.28,000/- = (Rs.14,000/- x 2) towards loss of income during laid up period.
f) Towards Future Earnings:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident he was inpatient in the hospital and has become permanently disabled.
The petitioner also examined Dr.ShaileshA.V.Rao working as an Neuro Surgeon, at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bengaluru as PW1.
This PW1 deposed that petitioner came to their hospital with history of RTA and sustained head injury.
As per wound certificate ExP9 the doctor has opined that the injuries sustained by petitioner are grievous in nature.
The PW1/Doctor has assessed the physical disability and to the whole body at 50% disability.

In order to prove his disability the doctor/PW1 has produced OPD records, Neuro (SCCH-9) 19 MVC.No.3841/2019 psychological assessment report and disability assessment guidelines which are marked at ExP1 to 3 respectively.

The petitioner contended that he was working as mason before accident., but not produced any document to show his avocation.
Therefore mere non producing of documents it cannot be said that the petitioner is not doing any work.
The PW1 assessed the whole body disability at 50%.

The petitioner (SCCH-9)

In order to prove the age of the petitioner he has produced Ex.P12/Aadhaar card, which shows that petitioner date of birth is as 01.01.1972.

Regarding Liability: As already stated above the petitioner has proved that the accident in question was caused by the driver of KSRTC Bus with rash and negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus.

At the time of argument the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has vehemently argued and submitted that there is a contributory negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle, he further submitted that at the time of accident there were 3 persons were riding in the motor cycle and there was a every chance of non control of the motor cycle by the rider while triple riding.
Therefore the (SCCH-9) 23 MVC.No.3841/2019 rider of the motor cycle has also contributed in causing the accident.

In this regard he relied upon judgments reported in ILR 2003 KAR 409 (P.Varalakshmi Reddy & Ors. V/s The Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation) and MFA 4193/2007 c/w 10454/07 (P.Anki Reddy & another V/s The Oriental Insurance & Ors. V/s Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd., & Ors.).

sentences.text: I have perused the entire materials available on record.
It is true that the PW.2 in her cross- examination has clearly admitted that there were 3 persons were riding in the motor cycle at the time of accident including her husband.
Even in the charge sheet vide Ex.P8 stated that one Chandrappa was the rider and Ramanna and Ranganatha were the pillion riders of the motor cycle TVS bearing No. KA-06-EM-122.
Therefore it appears that there were 3 persons were riding in the motor (SCCH-9) 24 MVC.No.3841/2019 cycle including the petitioner.
When there is triple riding it amounts to negligence and rider of such motor cycle definitely contributes in causing the accident.

In this regard I would like to rely upon the judgments reported in 1) 2004 (1) KLJ 498 (P.S.Somaiah & anr V/s The Director, Bangalore Dairy and Others),
wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that - If any rider of Motor cycle violates Sec.128 of M.V.Act moving in a triple riding then contributory negligence to be considered and compensation should be apportioned on the apportionment of negligence.

sentences.text: We are concerned as to whether such action of the individuals is permissible under law.
The motor cycle and any other two wheelers are meant only for two persons, the rider and a pillion rider.
If more than two persons are travelling in a motor cycle or any other two wheeler, undoubtedly such action of the individual would become illegal and un authorised.
It is an awful sight when we come across three persons travelling in a motor cycle.
They are sitting in such a cramped manner that the rider of the motor cycle almost sitting on the petrol tank or at the front edge of the seat.
When he was sitting in such a position, naturally because of the restricted movement of his legs, he cannot have the complete control over the brake.
The movements of his hands also so restricted.
When that be so, this court is of the opinion that definitely the rider of the two wheeler cannot have full control over the vehicle.

11. Apart from that, when three persons are travelling in a motor cycle, two as pillion riders, any unusual movement of the pillion riders would make the rider of the motor cycle to loose his control over the vehicle.

Even though such travelling of three persons in a motor cycle is contrary to the statute, still the enforcement wing do not care to take note of the same and failed to take action against their illegal action.
Virtually because of the failure on the (SCCH-9) 27 MVC.No.3841/2019 part of the enforcement wing, such travelling of three persons in the two wheelers has become a regular sight.
Even though the highway patroling is available but it is a rare sight to see a highway patrolling vehicle.
The travelling of three persons has become rampant in the mofussils and in the City; especially among the youngsters like the college students.
When that be the case, the enforcing authority is expected to enforce the statute with some strictness to avoid any untoward incident.
There is no purpose in conducting the Road Safety Week without infusing the road sense in compliance of the Rules and Regulations of the statute in the minds of those who are using the vehicles.

12. When three persons travelled in a motor cycle which is meant for two persons,
this court is of the view, the conduct of the persons who travelled in such a manner are liable for contributory negligence; especially when their action is contrary to the statute. "
20. As already stated above in this case the petitioner was riding as a pillion rider with other two persons is an admitted fact.
Riding motor cycle more than seating capacity amounts to a contributory negligence.

Therefore considering the law lay down in the aforesaid judgments and considering the contributory negligence of the vehicles in the case on hand, this tribunal has fixed Ramanna vs K.S.R.T.C on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136935816/

opennyai_summary.facts:
This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
Due to which petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
The petitioner has lost his earning capacity and cannot do his normal work prior to the accident.
The accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-06-F-1010.
The jurisdictional Police have registered a Criminal Case against the driver of KSRTC Bus in Cr.No.109/2019 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC.
The respondent being RC Owner and Insurer of the KSRTC Bus is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence,
petitioner constrained to file a petition for compensation.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1. Whether petitioner proves that on 27.04.2019 at about 11.30 a.m., petitioner was proceeding on a TVS vehicle bearing No.KA-060EM-122 as a pillion rider, the same was ridden by its rider from Sira Gate on the extreme left side on Old Nh-4 Sira Road with slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations, he reached at (SCCH-9) 7 MVC.No.3841/2019 Opposite to Maruthi Rice Mill, near Sridevi Hostel, Lingapura Tumkur at that time the suddenly the driver of KSRTC Bus,
bearing Reg.No.KA-06-F-1010 came in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing any of the traffic rule and regulations and dashed against the petitioner vehicle.
Due to impact, petitioner fell down and grievous injuries in the alleged ?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum of compensation?
from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the specific case of the petitioner that on 27.04.2019 at about 11.30 a.m., the (SCCH-9) 9 MVC.No.3841/2019 petitioner was met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 06-F-1010 while petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in TVS motor cycle bearing No.KA-06-EM-122 and sustained grievous injuries.
Ramanna vs K.S.R.T.C on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136935816/
4 10.
There is nothing on record to show this RW1 has filed (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.3841/2019 complaint against rider of motor cycle.
Therefore, only on self swearing statement it cannot be held that the accident was not caused by the driver of KSRTC Bus.
Apart from this in a claim petition arising out of the accident the proving of negligence of offending vehicle is only preponderance of probabilities and not standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt as required in criminal case.
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
However, it is quite natural that if any person admitted in the hospital he might have spent some amount towards conveyance.
Therefore,
considering the injuries and treatment taken by the petitioner this tribunal is of the (SCCH-9) 17 MVC.No.3841/2019 opinion that Rs.10,000/- is just and proper towards conveyance charges.
Hence the age of the petitioner is taken into consideration as 47 years for applying multiplier and the proper multiplier is "13" is applicable as per Smt. Sarala Verma's case.
As per the ratio laid down in Raj Kumar V/s Ajay Kumar and anr, this Tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his income.
Therefore, in the absence of positive documents about salary the notional income has to be considered.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.10,000/- is just and reasonable towards under the head of deprivation of future amenities.
Hence liability is fastened to the extent of 50% to the respondent No.1 in case court comes to the conclusion to award the compensation.
When there is triple riding it amounts to negligence and rider of such motor cycle definitely contributes in causing the accident.
2) 2003 (2) TAC 103 (Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Coimbatore Dvn) Ltd., Coimbatore V/s Abdul Salam & Others), wherein Hon'ble Madras High Court observed that riding the motor cycle more than seating capacity amounts to a negligence and contributory negligence be considered while awarding the compensation in accident case.
3) 2017 ACJ 418 (New India Assurance Co.., Ltd.,
V/s (SCCH-9) 25 MVC.No.3841/2019 Hemanth & Others), wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that- in case of triple riding there is a contributory negligence and liability to be fixed on apportionment to the insurance companies.
20. As already stated above in this case the petitioner was riding as a pillion rider with other two persons is an admitted fact.
Riding motor cycle more than seating capacity amounts to a contributory negligence.
